problems.name: Network Delay Time
problems.question: Given directed weighted edges times[i] = [u,v,w], n nodes labeled 1..n, and source k, return the time for all nodes to receive the signal, or -1 if any node is unreachable.
problems.constraints: 1 <= n <= 100; edge weights are positive; node labels are 1-based.

examples.explanation: Node 4 receives after path 2->3->4.
Node 1 is unreachable from 2.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O((n + E) log n); Space O(n + E). Dijkstra uses a min-heap adjacency list.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(number of explored walks with pruning); Space O(n + E + recursion depth). DFS prunes states not improving distance.

source.label: LeetCode 743 - Network Delay Time

problems.name: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
problems.question: Given flights [from,to,price], find the cheapest price from src to dst using at most k stops, or -1 if no route satisfies the stop limit.
problems.constraints: n <= 100; prices are positive; at most k + 1 edges may be used.

examples.explanation: 0->1->3 uses one stop.
The one-stop path is cheaper than direct.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O((k + 1)E); Space O(n). Bellman-Ford layers prevent same-round reuse.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O((k + 1)(n + E)) with memoization; Space O((k + 1)n + recursion depth).

source.label: LeetCode 787 - Cheapest Flights Within K Stops

problems.name: Path With Minimum Effort
problems.question: Given a heights grid, move 4-directionally from top-left to bottom-right while minimizing the maximum absolute height difference along the path.
problems.constraints: Grid size up to 100x100; height differences fit in int.

examples.explanation: A route exists where every step differs by at most 2.
The right-side route keeps max effort 1.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn log(mn)); Space O(mn). Dijkstra over grid cells with minimax relaxation.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn log W); Space O(mn). Binary search effort and recursive DFS reachability check.

source.label: LeetCode 1631 - Path With Minimum Effort

problems.name: Swim in Rising Water
problems.question: Given an n x n grid where grid[r][c] is the time that cell becomes passable, return the earliest time when a path exists from top-left to bottom-right.
problems.constraints: n <= 50; values are unique from 0 to n^2 - 1 in the original LeetCode problem.

examples.explanation: The destination opens at time 3.
The snake path is feasible when time reaches 16.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2 log n); Space O(n^2). Dijkstra minimizes the maximum grid value seen so far.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2 log W); Space O(n^2). Binary search the time and use recursive DFS for feasibility.

source.label: LeetCode 778 - Swim in Rising Water

problems.name: Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in MST
problems.question: Given an undirected weighted connected graph, return which edge indices are critical for every MST and which can appear in at least one MST.
problems.constraints: n <= 100 and edges <= 200 in the LeetCode problem; O(E^2 alpha(V)) classification is acceptable.

examples.explanation: Edges 0 and 1 are required in every MST.
Any three cycle edges can form an MST.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E^2 alpha(V) + E log E); Space O(E + V). Sorted Kruskal classification with DSU.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(E^2 alpha(V)); Space O(E + V). Recursive DSU find supports the same classification checks.

source.label: LeetCode 1489 - Find Critical and Pseudo-Critical Edges in MST

problems.name: Min Cost to Connect All Points
problems.question: Given points on a plane, connect all points with minimum total Manhattan distance cost.
problems.constraints: n <= 1000; complete graph has O(n^2) implicit edges.

examples.explanation: The minimum spanning tree has total cost 20.
Connect all three points with two cheapest useful edges.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n). Dense Prim keeps the best current connection for every outside point.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^2); Space O(n + recursion depth). Recursive Prim adds one point per call.

source.label: LeetCode 1584 - Min Cost to Connect All Points

problems.name: Optimize Water Distribution in a Village
problems.question: Given well costs for each house and pipe costs between houses, return the minimum cost to supply water to every house.
problems.constraints: n can be large enough that MST modeling is required; all costs are positive.

examples.explanation: Build well at house 1 and connect 1-2 and 2-3.
One well plus one pipe is cheapest.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O((n + p) log n); Space O(n + p). Prim starts from virtual source and chooses cheapest frontier edge.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O((n + p) log(n + p)); Space O(n + p). Recursive DSU find inside Kruskal.

source.label: LeetCode 1168 - Optimize Water Distribution in a Village

problems.name: Reconstruct Itinerary
problems.question: Given airline tickets [from,to], reconstruct the lexicographically smallest itinerary that starts at JFK and uses every ticket exactly once.
problems.constraints: All tickets belong to at least one valid itinerary in the LeetCode problem.

examples.explanation: ATL is chosen before SFO lexicographically.
Postorder handles the KUL dead end correctly.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E log E); Space O(E). Iterative Hierholzer uses min-heaps per airport and a stack.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(E log E); Space O(E). Recursive Hierholzer adds airports on postorder unwind.

source.label: LeetCode 332 - Reconstruct Itinerary

problems.name: Alien Dictionary
problems.question: Given sorted words from an alien language, return one valid character order, or empty string if the order is invalid.
problems.constraints: Characters are lowercase English letters in the common LeetCode version.

examples.explanation: Constraints imply w before e, e before r, r before t, t before f.
The constraints create a cycle.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(total characters + V + E); Space O(V + E). Kahn queue processes zero-indegree characters.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(total characters + V + E); Space O(V + E). DFS color states detect cycles and build reverse postorder.

source.label: LeetCode 269 - Alien Dictionary

problems.name: Course Schedule II
problems.question: Given numCourses and prerequisites [course, prerequisite], return an order to finish all courses or an empty array if impossible.
problems.constraints: Courses are labeled 0..numCourses-1; any valid topological order is accepted.

examples.explanation: Course 0 must come before 1.
The prerequisites form a cycle.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Kahn queue emits zero-indegree courses.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). DFS colors detect cycles and produce reverse postorder.

source.label: LeetCode 210 - Course Schedule II

problems.name: Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes
problems.question: Given an undirected connected graph, return the shortest number of edges needed to visit every node at least once.
problems.constraints: n <= 12 in the LeetCode problem, making bitmask states feasible.

examples.explanation: Start at a leaf, visit center and the other leaves.
A shortest walk can cover all nodes in four edges.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n * 2^n + E * 2^n); Space O(n * 2^n). BFS over (node, visitedMask).
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^3 + n^2 * 2^n); Space O(n * 2^n). Floyd distances plus recursive TSP memo.

source.label: LeetCode 847 - Shortest Path Visiting All Nodes

problems.name: Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time
problems.question: Given maxTime, undirected edges [u,v,time], and passingFees per city, return the minimum fee to reach city n-1 within maxTime or -1.
problems.constraints: maxTime <= 1000 in the LeetCode problem, so time-layer DP is feasible.

examples.explanation: Path 0-1-2-5 reaches in 30 with fee 11.
The cheaper path is too slow, so another route is needed.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(maxTime * E); Space O(maxTime * V). DP relaxes every edge between adjacent time layers.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V * maxTime + E * maxTime); Space O(V * maxTime). Memoized DFS chooses outgoing edges under remaining time.

source.label: LeetCode 1928 - Minimum Cost to Reach Destination in Time

problems.name: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors
problems.question: Given weighted undirected edges and a distance threshold, return the city with the fewest reachable cities within the threshold, breaking ties by larger city index.
problems.constraints: n <= 100 in the LeetCode problem; O(n^3) Floyd-Warshall is acceptable.

examples.explanation: City 3 has the smallest reachable count after tie-breaking.
City 0 reaches only city 1 within threshold.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(n^3); Space O(n^2). Floyd-Warshall computes all-pairs distances.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(n^3); Space O(n^3). Recursive shortest(i,j,k) memoizes allowed intermediate nodes.

source.label: LeetCode 1334 - Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors

problems.name: Critical Connections in a Network
problems.question: Given an undirected connected network, return all critical connections whose removal disconnects the graph.
problems.constraints: n up to 1e5; O(V + E) low-link traversal is required.

examples.explanation: Removing 1-3 isolates node 3.
The only edge is a bridge.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Tarjan low-link finds all bridges in one DFS.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Recursive DFS maintains discovery and low times.

source.label: LeetCode 1192 - Critical Connections in a Network

problems.name: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph
problems.question: Given n nodes and undirected edges, return the number of connected components.
problems.constraints: Nodes are labeled 0..n-1; DSU gives near-constant edge processing.

examples.explanation: Components are {0,1,2} and {3,4}.
All nodes are connected.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E alpha(V)); Space O(V). Union-Find maintains component count.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Recursive DFS counts components.

source.label: LeetCode 323 - Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph

problems.name: Kosaraju SCC Count
problems.question: Given a directed graph with n nodes and edges [u,v], return the number of strongly connected components.
problems.constraints: Use O(V + E) graph traversals; nodes are labeled 0..n-1.

examples.explanation: Every node reaches every other node.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Kosaraju uses finish order and reverse graph.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Recursive DFS performs both passes.

source.label: Kosaraju Algorithm - GeeksforGeeks

problems.name: Tarjan SCC Count
problems.question: Given a directed graph, count strongly connected components using one DFS pass with low-link values.
problems.constraints: O(V + E) time and space with nodes labeled 0..n-1.

examples.explanation: A DAG has each node as its own SCC.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Tarjan low-link processes SCCs in one DFS.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(V + E); Space O(V + E). Recursive low-link stack extraction.

source.label: Tarjan SCC Algorithm - GeeksforGeeks

problems.name: Minimum Spanning Tree Kruskal
problems.question: Given n nodes and undirected weighted edges [u,v,w], return the minimum spanning tree weight, or -1 if the graph is disconnected.
problems.constraints: Kruskal is O(E log E) and works when edges are given explicitly.

examples.explanation: Choose the first three edges.
Node 2 is disconnected.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E log E); Space O(V). Kruskal sorts once and uses DSU.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(E log E); Space O(V + E). Recursive scan accepts sorted edges with DSU.

source.label: Kruskal MST - CP Algorithms

problems.name: Minimum Spanning Tree Prim
problems.question: Given n nodes and undirected weighted edges, return the MST weight using Prim-style frontier expansion, or -1 if disconnected.
problems.constraints: Prim with adjacency heap runs in O(E log V).

examples.explanation: The frontier picks weights 1, 2, and 3.
Node 2 never enters the tree.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(E log V); Space O(V + E). Heap-based Prim tracks frontier edges.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(VE); Space O(V + recursion depth). Recursive dense Prim adds one node per call.

source.label: Prim MST - CP Algorithms

problems.name: Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
problems.question: Given a grid of 0 empty cells and 1 obstacles, return the minimum obstacles to remove to travel from top-left to bottom-right.
problems.constraints: Grid can be large; O(mn) 0-1 BFS is better than heap Dijkstra.

examples.explanation: Remove two obstacles along the best route.
A zero-obstacle path exists.

problems.optimizedComplexity: Time O(mn); Space O(mn). 0-1 BFS processes each directed grid edge a constant number of times.
problems.recursiveComplexity: Time O(mn * improvements); Space O(mn). Recursive relaxation prunes non-improving costs.

source.label: LeetCode 2290 - Minimum Obstacle Removal to Reach Corner
